blueprint_topic: Management of Care — evidence-based referral and interdisciplinary pulmonary rehabilitation for stable COPD
stem: A client with stable COPD reports exertional dyspnea and reduced activity tolerance. Which statement by the nurse best explains pulmonary rehabilitation?

options.A: It combines individualized exercise training with education and behavior-change support and can improve exercise capacity and health-related quality of life.
options.B: It focuses on inhaler adjustment and respiratory testing, while structured exercise is usually managed outside the rehabilitation program.
options.C: Its main goal is to improve spirometry values, so exercise training is useful primarily when lung-function measurements also improve.
options.D: It is generally started after hospitalization for a COPD exacerbation because stable COPD has insufficient evidence for routine participation.

rationale: A is correct. The current ATS pulmonary-rehabilitation guideline gives a strong recommendation, based on moderate-quality evidence, for participation in pulmonary rehabilitation by adults with stable COPD. ATS describes pulmonary rehabilitation as a comprehensive, patient-tailored, interdisciplinary intervention that includes exercise training, education, and behavior change; ATS also identifies improvements in exercise capacity/tolerance and health-related quality of life as established benefits. B is incorrect because structured exercise is a core component of pulmonary rehabilitation rather than an activity routinely managed outside the program. C is incorrect because pulmonary rehabilitation targets symptoms, function, exercise performance, autonomy, participation, and quality of life; its benefit is not contingent on a parallel improvement in spirometry. D is incorrect because ATS recommends pulmonary rehabilitation for stable COPD as well as after hospitalization for a COPD exacerbation.
educational_objective: Recognize pulmonary rehabilitation as an interdisciplinary, individualized exercise- and education/behavior-change intervention with guideline-supported benefit for adults with stable COPD.
source_organization: American Thoracic Society (ATS); National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_document_title: Pulmonary Rehabilitation for Adults with Chronic Respiratory Disease: An Official American Thoracic Society Clinical Practice Guideline; ATS Pulmonary Rehabilitation Assembly; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: Official ATS Clinical Practice Guideline published 2023-08-15 and still listed by ATS as the current pulmonary-rehabilitation clinical practice guideline when rechecked 2026-08-20; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: ATS guideline implementation page identifies Rochester et al., 'Pulmonary Rehabilitation for Adults with Chronic Respiratory Disease: An Official American Thoracic Society Clinical Practice Guideline,' AJRCCM 2023;208:e7-e26. ATS official 2023 guideline announcement, COPD Recommendation 1: adults with stable COPD should participate in pulmonary rehabilitation (strong recommendation, moderate-quality evidence); COPD Recommendation 2 separately recommends PR after hospitalization for exacerbation. Current ATS Pulmonary Rehabilitation Assembly page: PR is a comprehensive patient-tailored intervention including exercise training, education, and behavior change, delivered by an interdisciplinary team; it reduces symptoms and improves exercise tolerance and health-related quality of life; exercise training is a central evidence-based component. NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan Management of Care supports interdisciplinary collaboration, referral assessment, plan-of-care coordination, and resource utilization.
source_claim_supported: Current official ATS resources directly support PR's exercise/education/behavior-change components, interdisciplinary and individualized nature, strong recommendation for adults with stable COPD, and improvements in exercise capacity/tolerance and health-related quality of life. NCSBN supports the referral/care-coordination construct.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: collaborate with multidisciplinary team members, assess need for referrals, update the plan of care, and utilize resources to promote quality client care.
pdf_visual_verification: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan evidence was visually verified earlier in this cleanup session. ATS evidence used for Q1919 is current HTML; no ATS PDF evidence is used for the final claim set.
correction_summary: Original Q1919 had a 175-character correct answer versus 88-98 character distractors and an absolute-word cue. The stem and all four options were rebuilt to compare realistic misconceptions about pulmonary rehabilitation, with substantially balanced lengths and without absolute cueing. The final key tests program components, outcomes, and the stable-COPD guideline indication rather than recognition of cartoonishly false statements. Independent second-pass reread found no unresolved clinical, source, currentness, ambiguity, cueing, blueprint, or second-answer conflict.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly matches ATS definition/components and guideline-supported benefits for stable COPD.
option_audit.B: Plausible medication-centric misconception; incorrect because structured exercise is a core PR component, not normally external to the program.
option_audit.C: Plausible physiology-focused misconception; incorrect because PR benefit is functional and quality-of-life oriented and is not dependent on spirometric improvement.
option_audit.D: Plausible timing misconception; incorrect because ATS separately and strongly recommends PR for adults with stable COPD, not just after hospitalization.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on only/all/always/never/must-type absolute wording.
cueing_audit.answer_length: Final option lengths: A 157, B 138, C 133, D 142 characters; the correct answer is no longer uniquely conspicuous and the choices are substantially balanced.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives describe the purpose, components, or indication of pulmonary rehabilitation in parallel explanatory form.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: Independent adversarial reread found no defensible second answer. B misplaces a core exercise component, C incorrectly ties benefit to spirometric improvement, and D contradicts ATS's strong stable-COPD recommendation; A is uniquely best.

independent_second_pass: PASS — post-fetch adversarial reread independently rechecked stem, A/B/C/D, correct key, rationale, objective, current ATS guideline status, stable-COPD recommendation strength/quality, PR components and outcomes, NCSBN Management of Care fit, cueing and second-answer risk. The final item does not imply that PR replaces medication management or that benefit requires improved lung-function measurements. No unresolved conflict identified.
